# Merkel Cell Carcinoma of the Skin

**Authors:** Mary Brady, Yana Puckett

**Source:** StatPearls - StatPearls Publishing

## Abstract

Merkel cell carcinoma (MCC) is a rare and highly aggressive neuroendocrine tumor of the skin that most commonly arises on sun-exposed areas, particularly the head and neck, in older, fair-skinned males. Risk factors include exposure to ultraviolet (UV) radiation, advancing age, immunosuppression, and Merkel cell polyomavirus (MCPyV) infection.  A skin biopsy is diagnostic, and wide local excision with sentinel lymph node biopsy or therapeutic lymph node dissection is the surgical treatment for all patients diagnosed with MCC, as the disease typically has a rapidly progressive course. Treatment involves wide local excision with or without adjuvant radiotherapy for local disease. Recent studies have explored the role of neoadjuvant immune checkpoint inhibitors in MCC. Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) is an emerging MCC surveillance tool following initial treatment.
